PLUG AND

SPECIFICATION FOR RING GAUGES FOR SELF HOLDING ( First Revision )

TAPERS

1. Scope

- Covers the requirements of taper plug and taper ring gauges used for verification of internal and external self holding tapers conforming to IS : 1715-1986 `Dimensions for selt-hulding tapers ( second revision ) `. 1.1 Recommendations

for the use of gauges are given in Appendix

A.

2; Types
2.1 Taper Plug Gauge Plain -

2.2 Taper Plug Gauge Tanged 2.3 Taper Ring Gauge Plain 2.4 Taper Ring Gauge Tanged 3. Material
3.1 Material and Hardness

as T215Cr12 for gauges:

3.2 Hardness - The gauges shall be suitably heat treated for hardness and stabilized. The gauging surfaces shall have hardness of 760 HV ( Min ) [ see iS : 1501 ( Part 1 )-1984 `Method for Vickers hardness test for metallic materials : Part 1 HV5 to HVIOO ( second revision )I'. 4. Dimensions

6. Designation 6.1 The designation of taper plug or ring gauge shall indicate: a) Type of the gauge; b) Designation of taper; and c) Number of this standard. Examples

a) A taper plug gauge, plain for inspecting
end shanks shall be designated as:

sockets having

Morse taper 4 for tapped or plain

b)

Taper Plug Gauge, Plain MT4 - IS : 2251 A taper ring gauge, plain for inspecting tapped or `plain end shanks 100 shall be designated as: Taper Ring Gauge, Plain ME 100 - IS : 2251 designated plug gauge, tanged for inspecting as: Taper Plug Gauge, Tanged sockets MT 6 having IS : 2251 Morse

7. Marking 7.1 The gauges shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the designation manufacturer's name, initials or recognised trade-n,ark and the year of manufacture. 7.2 It is recommended identification. 7.3 Certification that gauges should Details also be marked with a serial number Standards.

of

the

taper,

which

facilitates

Marking

available

with the Bureau of Indian

gauges shall be covered with a suitable rust proof 8. Protective Coating and Packing -The coating and packed in non-absorbent paper. The gauges shall then be packed in suitable boxes for safe handling. Each type and size of gauge shall be packed separately and the cover shall bear the type and size of gauge, manufacturer's name, initials and the year of manufacture.

APPENDIX ( Clause 1.l ) RECOMMENDATIONS

A

FOR USE OF GAUGES

A-l. Taper Plug Gauge, Plain - The internal taper shall be inspected by the help of taper plug gauge, plain. The taper plug gauge, plain shall be inserted as far as it goes with light pressure. At the extreme point, the face of large end of the internal taper shall be within two steps provided on the taper plug gauge, plain (see Fig. 1 ).

A-3. Taper Ring Gauge, Plain - The external taper of plain or tapped end shank inspected with the help of a taper ring gauge, plain. The taper ring gauge, plain inserted as far as it goes with light pressure. At the extreme position, the small end shank under test shall be flush or short of face of the ring gauge on the Small end. This verified with the help of a straight edge ( see Fig. 3 ).

A-4. Taper Ring Gauge, Tanged - The external taper of tanged end shank shall be inspected by the help of the taper ring gauge, tanged. The tapering gauge, tanged shall be inserted as far as it goes with light pressure. At the extreme position, no part of tang under test shall extend beyond the sufaces A, B and C as shown in Fig. 4. The shank surfaces may however be flush with these sufaces.
